about: Is Sonnet 5.5 good enough to make the studio's films? The same four prompts made by the same studio code (one tree), once on Opus 5.5 and once on Sonnet 5.5, both at effort xhigh, then read blind by the same Opus grader. Four use cases, none over a minute: a product launch, an explainer about a real company (web research, its own logo), a 60 s collage motion-graphics piece, and a children's bedtime story. Asked 2026-10-02.

prompts.audience: adults: owners of small businesses, a product launch
prompts.prompt: A 30-second launch video for Brightfold, a new app for small businesses: snap a photo of a receipt and Brightfold files it, matches it to the right line on the bank statement, and closes your books at the end of the month. The audience is owners of businesses with 5 to 50 people, who dread month-end and the shoebox of receipts. Make it look like a polished product launch from a top software company: the app's screens, the receipts flying into place, the month closing itself. End on the name Brightfold and the line "Close your month in minutes." Brightfold is a made-up company for a showcase: no prices, customer names or statistics.

prompts.audience: adults: a general audience, a company's product
prompts.prompt: A short explainer about Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver: what it is, why it is fast and private, and how to switch to it.

prompts.audience: adults: a portfolio piece for social video
prompts.prompt: Create a 60 second motion graphic explainer video about the history of ice cream from the inception, to present day. The art style should be newspaper cutout / mixed media aesthetic with a high degree of polish. This piece is for your portfolio, so make sure to make it great.
A bedtime story about a lighthouse keeper's cat who is afraid of the dark, until one stormy night.
